title: Treasury Announces Form 990 Transparency Initiative to Expose Hidden Funding and Strengthen Oversight
summary: The Treasury Department announced on April 23, 2026 that the IRS plans to revise Form 990 to improve transparency for tax-exempt organizations under section 501(c)(3), focusing on government contracts, grants, and fiscal sponsorship arrangements. The initiative aims to detect misconduct, reduce fraud and abuse, and increase public accountability for organizations receiving public funds or tax-deductible donations.
key_points: IRS plans to revise Form 990 to improve transparency for 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations
Changes target government contracts, government grants, and fiscal sponsorship arrangements
Treasury and IRS will publish proposed regulations with public comment opportunity before finalization
Changes aim to make it harder for organizations to obscure who controls funds and how they are used
Proposed changes will consider administrative feasibility, proportionality, and reporting burden
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated: 'Public money and tax-exempt status demand public accountability'
why_it_matters: This initiative affects nonprofit organizations receiving government funding or tax-deductible donations. Increased reporting requirements could impose greater compliance burdens on fiscal sponsors and 501(c)(3) organizations. However, this is a tax administration and regulatory matter with no direct connection to financial market structure or macro-level economic catalysts.
